Dr. Sayers, who has thankfully left, never seemed like he wanted to be there. It felt like he was just going through the motions—Googling symptoms, looking up treatments, and even outright saying he didn’t want to do the job. He also had the audacity to tell me that my job was much easier than his, and I know for a fact I’m not the only one he said that to.

It wasn’t just one bad experience; there was a clear pattern of neglect that affected me, my partner, my father-in-law, and several friends. We all ended up having to go private, despite paying our taxes for a service we should be able to rely on.

To make matters worse, one of the receptionists is incredibly rude over the phone—zero social skills, never identifies herself, and acts like she’s doing you a favor. If you can’t make the appointment she offers due to work or other commitments, she huffs, puffs, and speaks with a horrible attitude.

I really don’t understand how this place is run. Everyone has stress in their lives, but if you work in healthcare, I’d like to believe it’s because you actually care about people. Usk GP doesn’t give that impression at all. That said, some of the staff do seem lovely—it’s just a shame a small handful ruin the experience for everyone else. If you’re that fed up with your job, just leave. But I guess an easy Monday-to-Friday paycheck is hard to walk away from.

Wouldn’t recommend this practice to All the Doctors are lovely,  but I find Dr Parry suits my personality best. For each patient it may be a different Doctor.  In fact the receptionist staff are all lovely and do not fit the stereotype. Tolerant when I am not at my best. What is worrying to me is the new system where you can only make same day appointments. I would like to make book ahead appointments to discuss my chronic health problems. The same day telephone triage system works well for acute issues but not so well for those with chronic problems or for those who need to make arrangements to get to the surgery.  The appointment system should be able to accommodate book ahead appointments for those that have complex medical conditions and prefer to have continuity of care.  It feels like a family practice and I feel cared for when I visit there. Well Done.
